# Indefinite Lattice Algorithms

Reference for all methods in this repo that handle **indefinite** symmetric bilinear
forms (any signature, not necessarily positive-definite).

> Contrast: the entire `LatticeStabEquiCan` → `InvariantVectorFamily` → `Shvec_exact`
> → `SHORT_*` pipeline is **positive-definite only** (it relies on a closest-vector
> solver that requires positive-definite Gram matrices, and the classic LLL
> implementation asserts positive-definiteness).

---

## Mathematical background

### Quadratic forms and orthogonal groups

Let G be a symmetric n × n integer matrix with nonzero determinant. This defines a
**quadratic form** Q on ℤⁿ by Q(v) = vᵀGv. The value Q(v) is the **norm** of v.
The pair L = (ℤⁿ, G) is a **lattice** with Gram matrix G.

The **orthogonal group** of L, written O(L), is

> O(L) = { g ∈ GLₙ(ℤ) : gᵀGg = G },

where **GLₙ(ℤ)** denotes the group of invertible n × n integer matrices
(det g = ±1), and gᵀ is the transpose.

Two forms with Gram matrices G₁ and G₂ are **equivalent** if ∃ g ∈ GLₙ(ℤ) such
that gᵀG₁g = G₂. Two vectors v₁, v₂ in the same lattice lie in the same
**O(L)-orbit** if ∃ g ∈ O(L) with g·v₁ = v₂.

### Totally isotropic subspaces

A subspace W ⊂ ℚⁿ is **totally isotropic** (with respect to Q) if Q(w) = 0 for all
w ∈ W. Equivalently, w₁ᵀGw₂ = 0 for all w₁, w₂ ∈ W — the form vanishes identically
on W. The maximal dimension of such a subspace is the **Witt index** of Q. For a
form of signature (p, q) with p ≥ q, the Witt index equals q.

A **totally isotropic flag** is a chain W₁ ⊂ W₂ ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ Wₖ of totally isotropic
subspaces with dim Wᵢ = i.

### The positive cone and hyperbolic geometry

When Q has signature (n − 1, 1), the set

> C⁺ = { x ∈ ℝⁿ : Q(x) > 0 }

has two connected components (the sheets of a two-sheeted hyperboloid). Fixing one
sheet, O(L) acts on it isometrically for the hyperbolic metric on the
hyperboloid model of ℍⁿ⁻¹.

### Fundamental domain

A **reflection** in O(L) is an element of order 2 that fixes a hyperplane
pointwise and sends some vector r (a **root**) to −r. The roots occurring in
practice may have any negative norm (−2, −4, −6, …); there is no restriction to
−2 roots.

The **discrete reflection subgroup** W ≤ O(L) is the subgroup generated by all
reflections whose roots appear as walls of the fundamental domain. The edgewalk
computes these walls explicitly: at each vertex v of the domain, the rows of
`vert.MatRoot` are the normal vectors of the simple roots at v, and W is built
as the permutation group generated by the reflections in all such roots discovered
during the walk.

A **fundamental domain** for the action of W on the chosen sheet of C⁺ is a closed
polyhedral cone D ⊂ C⁺ such that:

1. Every W-orbit in C⁺ intersects D.
2. For g ≠ 1 in W, the interiors of D and g·D are disjoint.
3. Each bounding hyperplane of D is the mirror of a simple reflection generating W.

The **Vinberg algorithm** (edgewalking) computes D iteratively: from an initial
vertex and known walls, it walks edges of the cone, discovering new walls until
the domain closes (finite covolume) or a cusp is detected.

### Perfect forms

A quadratic form Q is **perfect** if it is uniquely determined up to positive
scaling by its set of **minimal vectors**

> M(Q) = { v ∈ ℤⁿ \ {0} : Q(v) > 0 is minimal }.

Concretely, Q is perfect iff the rank-one matrices vvᵀ for v ∈ M(Q) span the full
space of symmetric n × n matrices. Equivalently, the only solutions (X, λ) to

> vᵀXv = λ  for all v ∈ M(Q)

are positive scalar multiples of (G, c), where c is the minimal positive value of
Q.

Voronoi proved that in each dimension there are finitely many GLₙ(ℤ)-classes of
perfect positive-definite forms, and that they tile the cone of positive-definite
forms: every positive-definite form lies in the closure of a unique **perfect
cone** (the convex cone spanned by one perfect form).

The same definition extends to Lorentzian and general indefinite forms. In the
Lorentzian case the geometry is hyperbolic and there may be infinitely many
perfect forms.

### Critical set

The **critical set** of Q is M(Q) regarded as a finite subset of ℤⁿ modulo v ∼ −v.
"Starting from a critical set" means: given the minimal vectors of a perfect form,
recover its Gram matrix G by solving vᵀGv = const for all v in the set.

### Flipping (wall-crossing)

The **flipping algorithm** (Voronoi's algorithm) enumerates all perfect forms by
walking between neighbours. Two perfect forms are neighbours if their perfect
cones share a facet. Given a perfect form Q and an outer normal to a facet of its
cone, the algorithm replaces one minimal vector with another to produce the
adjacent perfect form.

### Reduction

A Gram matrix G is **reduced** if it has been transformed by some g ∈ GLₙ(ℤ) into
gᵀGg in a form that makes the arithmetic structure of the lattice transparent:
entries are small, short vectors are visible as basis elements or short
combinations, and isotropic subspaces (when they exist) are exposed as coordinate
subspaces. In this codebase, reduction is performed by Denis Simon's indefinite
LLL algorithm (`Indefinite_LLL.h`), which extends the classical LLL algorithm to
forms of arbitrary signature. A form is called **full-dimensional** if it is
nondegenerate (trivial radical), so that the algorithm can work directly on the
entire space rather than splitting off a nullspace complement.

### Naming convention: `_Kernel` suffix

Methods with a `_Kernel` suffix (e.g. `INDEF_FORM_AutomorphismGroup_Kernel`,
`LORENTZ_GetGeneratorsAutom_Kernel`) are internal implementation routines that
do the actual computation. The non-`_Kernel` wrappers handle preprocessing
(reduction, signature classification) and postprocessing before or after calling
the `_Kernel` routine. There is no algebraic "kernel" involved — this is purely
a code-level naming convention.

## 1. General indefinite forms — `src_indefinite/CombinedAlgorithms.h`

Entry point: `CombinedIndefiniteAlgorithms<T, Tint, Tgroup>`. Dispatches by
signature using `IndefiniteReduction` from `Indefinite_LLL.h`.

### Automorphism groups

| Method | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `INDEF_FORM_AutomorphismGroup(Q)` | O(L) — the integral orthogonal group |
| `INDEF_FORM_AutomorphismGroup_Reduced(Q)` | Same, after reduction to a nondegenerate block; handles the nullspace by splitting it off and extending the result back |
| `INDEF_FORM_AutomorphismGroup_FullDim(Q)` | Same, for a nondegenerate form — applies approximate canonical reduction then computes the group |
| `INDEF_FORM_AutomorphismGroup_Kernel(Q)` | Core implementation: dispatches by signature (definite / Lorentzian / general indefinite) |

### Vector stabilizers

| Method | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `INDEF_FORM_StabilizerVector(Q, v)` | Stab_{O(L)}(v) — generators of the stabilizer of v |
| `INDEF_FORM_StabilizerVector_Reduced(Q, v)` | Same, assumes Q has already been reduced by `IndefiniteReduction` |
| `INDEF_FORM_StabilizerVector_NotReduced(Q, v)` | Same, but performs the reduction internally first |

### Vector equivalence and orbit representatives

| Method | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `INDEF_FORM_EquivalenceVector(Q₁, Q₂, v₁, v₂)` | Tests ∃ g ∈ GLₙ(ℤ) : gᵀG₁g = G₂ and g·v₁ = v₂ |
| `INDEF_FORM_GetOrbitRepresentative(Q, X)` | Orbit reps for {v : Q(v) = X} under O(L) |
| `INDEF_FORM_TestEquivalence(Q₁, Q₂)` | Tests GLₙ(ℤ)-equivalence of two forms |

### Isotropic subspaces

| Method | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `INDEF_FORM_Stabilizer_IsotropicKplane(Q, W)` | Stab_{O(L)}(W) for a k-dim totally isotropic subspace W |
| `INDEF_FORM_Stabilizer_IsotropicKflag(Q, F)` | Stab_{O(L)}(F) for a totally isotropic flag F |
| `INDEF_FORM_RightCosets_IsotropicKplane(Q, W)` | Right coset reps for Stab_{O(L)}(W) in O(L) |
| `INDEF_FORM_RightCosets_IsotropicKflag(Q, F)` | Same for a flag |
| `INDEF_FORM_GetOrbit_IsotropicKplane(Q, k)` | Orbit reps for totally isotropic k-planes under O(L) |
| `INDEF_FORM_GetOrbit_IsotropicKflag(Q, k)` | Orbit reps for isotropic flags under O(L) |

## 2. Lorentzian forms — `src_lorentzian/`

All methods assume signature (n − 1, 1).

The key algorithmic difference from the general indefinite methods is how O(L)
is computed: `INDEF_FORM_AutomorphismGroup` uses indefinite reduction and
approximate models built from short vectors, while `LORENTZ_GetGeneratorsAutom`
uses perfect form enumeration (Voronoi flipping) to walk the graph of perfect
cones and extract generators from the resulting database. Perfect form
enumeration is only implemented for the Lorentzian signature.

Additionally, the Lorentzian section provides edgewalking (`LORENTZ_RunEdgewalkAlgorithm`),
which computes the fundamental domain of the reflection subgroup W ≤ O(L) — a
construction specific to hyperbolic space.

### Automorphism groups — `lorentzian_perfect.h`

| Method | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `LORENTZ_ComputeStabilizer(G, eFamEXT)` | Stabilizer of a perfect form, given its Gram matrix G and the matrix of extremal vectors eFamEXT; returns both matrix generators and the permutation action on those vectors |
| `LORENTZ_GetGeneratorsAutom(G)` | Generators of O(L) |
| `LORENTZ_GetGeneratorsAutom_Reduced(G, data)` | Same, for a form already in reduced shape |
| `LORENTZ_GetGeneratorsAutom_Kernel(G)` | Core implementation, without preprocessing |

### Orbit representatives

| Method | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `LORENTZ_GetOrbitRepresentative(G, X)` | Orbit reps for {v : Q(v) = X} under O(L) |
| `LORENTZ_GetOrbitRepresentative_Kernel(G, X)` | Internal implementation, without preprocessing |

### Equivalence and isomorphism

| Method | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `LORENTZ_TestEquivalenceMatrices(G₁, G₂)` | GLₙ(ℤ)-equivalence of two Lorentzian forms |
| `LORENTZ_TestEquivalence(G₁, info₁, G₂, info₂)` | Equivalence with full vertex data |
| `LORENTZ_TestEquivalenceMatrices_Reduced(G₁, G₂)` | Same, on reduced forms |

### Edgewalk (Vinberg algorithm) — `edgewalk.h`

| Method | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `LORENTZ_RunEdgewalkAlgorithm(G, vertexInfo)` | Fundamental domain of W ≤ O(L) acting on C⁺ |
| `LORENTZ_RunEdgewalkAlgorithm_Isomorphism(data₁, v₁, data₂, v₂)` | Tests equivalence of two fundamental domains |
| `LORENTZ_RunEdgewalkAlgorithm_Kernel(G, vertexInfo, …)` | Internal implementation, with user-supplied callbacks |

### Stabilizer generators from the fundamental domain — `fund_domain_vertices.h`

| Method | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `LORENTZ_GetStabilizerGenerator(G, vertexInfo)` | Stabilizer of a vertex of the fundamental domain |

### Positive-norm vector search

| Method | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `LORENTZ_FindPositiveVectors(G, v)` | Vectors with Q(v) > 0, seeded from v |
| `LORENTZ_SearchInitialVector(G, …)` | Seed vector for perfect-form enumeration |

### Perfect-form enumeration (Voronoi flipping) — `lorentzian_perfect.h`

| Method | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `LORENTZ_Kernel_Flipping(G, …)` | One flipping step across a facet (core implementation) |
| `LORENTZ_DoFlipping(G, …)` | Full flipping walk to enumerate all perfect forms |
| `LORENTZ_GetOnePerfect(G, criticalSet)` | Reconstructs G from its critical set M(Q) |

## 3. Indefinite lattice reduction — `src_isotropy/Indefinite_LLL.h`

| Method | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `IndefiniteReduction(M)` | Reduces any symmetric form via Denis Simon's indefinite LLL + block decomposition |
| `Indefinite_LLL(M)` | Core indefinite LLL subroutine |
| `ComputeReductionIndefinite(M, look_for_isotropic)` | Same, with isotropic vector search |
| `SimpleIndefiniteReduction(M)` | Lightweight reduction via I + α·Eᵢⱼ |
| `LLLIndefiniteReduction(M)` | LLL-based variant |

## 4. Positive-norm vector search — `src_isotropy/Positivity.h`

| Method | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `INDEFINITE_GetShortPositiveVector(G)` | v ∈ ℤⁿ with G(v, v) > 0 and G(v, v) minimal |
| `GetShortIntegralVector(G, bound, strict)` | v ∈ ℤⁿ with 0 < G(v, v) < bound |

## 5. Quick decision guide

| Task | Positive-definite method | Indefinite method |
|---|---|---|
| **Orbit of v under O(L)** | ❌ Only via short-vector enumeration | `INDEF_FORM_GetOrbitRepresentative(Q, X)` |
| **Stab_{O(L)}(v)** | ❌ Definite-only pipeline | `INDEF_FORM_StabilizerVector(Q, v)` |
| **Stab under general matrix group G** | `GetStabilizerWeightMatrix` | `MatrixIntegral_Stabilizer_General` or `LinearSpace_Stabilizer` |
| **O(L) = Aut(L)** | `ArithmeticAutomorphismGroup` | `INDEF_FORM_AutomorphismGroup(Q)` |
| **v₁ ~ v₂ under O(L)** | ❌ Definite-only pipeline | `INDEF_FORM_EquivalenceVector(Q₁, Q₂, v₁, v₂)` |
| **Q₁ ≅ Q₂** | `ArithmeticEquivalence` | `INDEF_FORM_TestEquivalence(Q₁, Q₂)` |
